subsystems.name: Targeting and navigation
subsystems.role: gets the units to the damaged tissue instead of everywhere else.
parts: surface ligands that bind specific cell markers

subsystems.name: Molecular machinery
subsystems.role: the tiny moving parts that do work — open, close, cut, bond or fold.
parts: light- or chemically driven molecular motors

subsystems.name: Payload and repair chemistry
subsystems.role: the actual rebuilding: enzymes and nucleic acids that add, remove or rejoin molecules.

subsystems.name: Power and fuel
subsystems.role: no battery fits at this scale, so energy must come from chemistry or from outside the body.
parts: catalytic use of glucose or ATP

subsystems.name: Control and communication
subsystems.role: coordinates thousands of units so they act together rather than randomly.
parts: logic circuits encoded in DNA or RNA

subsystems.name: Safety and clearance
subsystems.role: keeps the swarm from being attacked by the immune system or lingering forever.
parts: stealth coatings such as PEG or lipids

buildSteps.title: Design the components in software
buildSteps.detail: Protein and nucleic-acid structures are designed so they fold and assemble predictably, tested first as simulations and then as small synthesised samples.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the parts
buildSteps.detail: DNA strands are made by solid-phase chemical synthesis, proteins by engineered cells, and inorganic cores by nanoparticle self-assembly.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise each part
buildSteps.detail: Targeting molecules, catalysts and payloads are attached by selective coupling chemistry, and the loading of each is measured.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: Parts are combined into a single unit and coated in lipid or polymer for immune stealth, then imaged by cryo-electron microscopy to check the structure.

buildSteps.title: Test on tissue models
buildSteps.detail: Organoids and microfluidic tissue chips show whether the units reach the right cells and do more good than harm.

buildSteps.title: Animal studies
buildSteps.detail: Biodistribution, dosing, immune response and clearance are measured in animals before any human exposure.

buildSteps.title: Human trials in a narrow indication
buildSteps.detail: The first human use would be a small, well-defined repair task — not whole-organ rebuilding — tested for safety first.

buildSteps.title: Scale up manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Batch synthesis, sterility and quality control must hold for billions of identical units; this is a chemistry and factory problem as much as a science one.

prerequisites.why: work on switching and rotating single molecules won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2016, but these machines do not build tissue.
folded DNA structures can be made to order, though not yet as autonomous repair devices inside a body.
lipid nanoparticles and antibody-drug conjugates reach specific tissues in some approved medicines — the closest real precedent.
cells can be engineered to sense a signal and respond, but the logic is simple and hard to keep stable.

prerequisites.tech: Molecular-resolution sensing inside a living body
prerequisites.why: nothing clinically available can watch millions of units and confirm what each one is doing in real time.
we cannot yet instruct a body to rebuild a complex organ, regardless of the tools used.

pathway.milestone: nanomedicines that already work: lipid-nanoparticle RNA delivery, antibody-drug conjugates, engineered cell therapies
pathway.unlocks: proof that engineered particles and cells can act precisely in a patient.

pathway.milestone: programmed cells and gene editing used as living therapies
pathway.unlocks: treatments that sense a condition and respond biologically, though each is designed for one disease.

pathway.milestone: molecular machines performing useful assembly on non-living surfaces in the lab
pathway.unlocks: evidence that molecular-scale manufacturing can be controlled outside biology.

pathway.milestone: limited in-body repair tasks (closing a small wound, clearing one deposit) rather than whole-organ rebuilding
pathway.unlocks: a realistic first use case and a regulatory path.
